findings.summary: LIST endpoint does not scope by user at all -- findManyByUserId never uses its userId parameter. Verified live: both users' 60-item lists were identical and each contained the other's freshly-created garment. Read the exact broken line in wardrobe.repository.ts and quoted it.
Persistence holds; separately noted AC2's 'retention policy' has no actual implementation (no expiry field/mechanism anywhere) -- same documentation-gap observation as the clean-round self-eval.

note: SELF-EVALUATOR ALSO CAUGHT THE MUTATION, correctly and precisely, including quoting the exact broken source line. This means D-001 is NOT a unique independent-evaluator catch under the H0 definition (detection in fewer than two of three self-evaluator reps required for uniqueness -- self caught it in its one rep). Honest, real result: this particular defect did not discriminate between the two conditions. Both were effective, likely because this self-evaluator prompt explicitly required actual black-box HTTP exercise, not just code review.
